one_line: Kerala astronomer-mathematician of Alathiyur who refined planetary tables through eclipse observations and authored Drigganita, Grahanamandana and Goladipika in the 15th century.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s, slim but sturdy, a contemplative scholar with the quiet physicality of someone accustomed to nightly sky-watching.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown Kerala complexion, gently arched brows, sharp yet kind eyes, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache, and a calm, focused default expression as if mid-calculation.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled back into a modest low knot at the nape, front kept smooth with a slight center part, adorned with a simple off-white cotton headband tied snugly around the forehead.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate Kerala Brahmin attire: an off-white handwoven cotton upper cloth (uttariya) draped over both shoulders and crossing the chest, worn over a long cream-colored dhoti/mundu that falls to the ankles and is pleated in front, faint pale-gold border along the dhoti edge, bare arms but fully clothed torso by wrapping style, a thin sacred thread (yajnopavita) diagonally across the chest still mostly covered by the uttariya folds; simple leather sandals on his feet, and minimal jewelry limited to a small copper bangle on the right wrist and a humble beaded waist cord barely visible under the uttariya; textiles look slightly coarse, village-made, with very subtle vertical weave textures but no bright patterns.
appearance.signature: A palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cotton cord, accompanied by a small wooden stylus and a compact hand-carved wooden gnomon-sundial block, carried together as his astronomer’s kit.

ref_desc: Vatasseri Parameśvara is a late-40s medium-brown Kerala scholar with an oval face, low-knot black hair and off-white headband, wearing cream dhoti with pale-gold border and off-white uttariya, copper wrist bangle, and carrying red-tied palm-leaf manuscripts with stylus and small wooden gnomon-sundial, in an off-white, cream, pale-gold, medium-brown and red palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Vatasseri Parameśvara: a late-40s Kerala astronomer with medium-brown complexion, oval face, calm thoughtful eyes, straight nose and neat moustache, black hair pulled into a low knot at the nape, front parted slightly and wrapped with a simple off-white cotton headband. He wears era-accurate 15th-century Kerala Brahmin clothing: an off-white handwoven cotton upper cloth (uttariya) draped over both shoulders and crossing the chest to keep the torso modestly covered, and a long cream-colored dhoti/mundu reaching the ankles with soft pleats in front and a pale-gold border along the hem. A thin sacred thread runs diagonally under the uttariya folds, and his arms are bare but dignified; he has a small copper bangle on his right wrist and simple sandals on his feet. His signature astronomer’s kit is a bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tied with a red cotton cord, together with a small wooden stylus and a compact hand-carved wooden gnomon-sundial block that he holds or has at his side. Use an off-white, cream, pale-gold, medium-brown and red colour palette, and show him from multiple angles to emphasize the consistent face, low-knot hairstyle with headband, dhoti with gold border, draped uttariya and the red-tied palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus and wooden gnomon-sundial.
